key_insight: Recursive, weight-sharing transformers can outperform overparameterized standard transformers for small engineering surrogate datasets by trading extra compute for far fewer learnable parameters.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for thermo-mechanical reliability workflows in semiconductor package design, where repeated finite element analyses are expensive and low-dimensional design spaces favor compact surrogates.
method: Compared three recursive transformer variants: Tiny Recursive Model, Depth Recursive transformer, and a simple recursive transformer.
Evaluated hardware-aware tradeoffs using predictive metrics, parameter count, and FLOPs.
Tested on thermo-mechanical package reliability and a Laplace PDE capacitance solver.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic comparison on two low-dimensional engineering tasks using Recall, Mean Reciprocal Rank, parameter count, and FLOPs to assess accuracy versus efficiency.
watch_item: Recursive models may still be constrained by the quality and coverage of the small training dataset, so careful validation is needed to avoid misleading gains from compactness alone.
paper_title: Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability
